originalTitle: Ukraine war briefing: F-16 crashes while chasing Russian air targets
summary: Pilot found safe and taken for medical treatment after ‘malfunction’; Russian drone company chief shot. What we know on day 1,618
content: An F-16 fighter jet crashed on a frontline mission with its pilot ejecting safely, Ukraine’s air force announced on Wednesday. The aircraft ‌was on duty intercepting Russian airborne targets when it malfunctioned. The pilot was ‌found safe and taken for medical treatment. Experts were examining the crash site. Ukraine has received F-16s from Nato countries including the Netherlands and Denmark. The director and founder of a Russian drone manufacturer was shot and wounded early on Wednesday in what prosecutors described as an “attempted murder”. Andrei Cherezov is head of the Russian Air Transport Laboratory, most famous for developing the “Ovod” family of combat drones. Cherezov was returning home from work at about 1am when he was attacked by an unknown assailant in Tula, about 150km (90 miles) south of Moscow, Russia’s Izvestia newspaper reported. Ukrainian forces hit two of Russia’s biggest oil refineries over Tuesday night: a Lukoil refinery in Russia’s Perm region, more than 1,500km (900 miles) from Ukraine, and a refinery in Ryazan, about 400km (180 miles) from the border. Ukraine’s security service and military general staff announced the strikes. The refineries have a combined annual production capacity of around 220m barrels of oil, according to Ukraine. The Russian online retailer Wildberries, which Ukraine has targeted in recent days, said it evacuated employees from a facility in Ryazan. Russia’s largest ⁠lender, Sberbank, is scrambling to restructure loans and cover lending losses because of Ukrainian drone attacks on the e-commerce company. Sberbank said the credit quality of online retailers and vendors had deteriorated following the attacks, with ⁠about 300 companies seeking to restructure loans. Sberbank lends to both Wildberries and rival Ozon, whose facilities have ‌not been targeted. The Russian rouble weakened by another 1.9% against the US ⁠dollar on Wednesday ⁠to its lowest since 3 April, market data showed. It has fallen by 14% against the dollar since ‌20 May, and has also fallen against the Chinese yuan, Russia’s most traded foreign currency. Ukrainian units have struck 201 Russian vessels over the past three weeks in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov, which border both countries, a senior military official said. The tally does not include vessels hit by Ukraine’s security service and other military groups. Ukrainian forces also struck a naval base used by Russia’s Black Sea, according to the military general staff. It reported other strikes on a radar station in Russia’s Bryansk region on the border and on a drone launch site and a road bridge in the occupied part of Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region. Russian glide bombs struck the Ukrainian city of Kharkiv and 17 other places in the region of the same name over the previous 24 hours, wounding 11 people, said the head of the regional military administration, Oleh Syniehubov, on Wednesday. In Ukraine’s Kherson a man was killed and another three people injured in a Russian drone attack, local authorities said. Russian officials have charged Pavel Durov, the founder and chief executive of the messaging app Telegram, with aiding terrorism. The 41-year-old Russian-born billionaire, who lives in the UAE, has proven adept at resisting Kremlin efforts to bring the internet and digital communications under its control. Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) accuses Telegram of failing to remove “numerous channels, chats and bots” allegedly used by Ukrainian agencies and organisations against Russia. Russian journalist Darya Shipacheva pleaded guilty to ⁠treason at a Moscow court and was sentenced on Wednesday to 12 ⁠years in ⁠a penal colony, the Interfax news agency reported. The charges stemmed ‌from an ‌alleged money transfer to Ukraine, Interfax said. According to Mediazona, Shipacheva specialised in science and medical journalism and worked for several prominent Russian media organisations. The Committee to Protect Journalists says at least 29 journalists are imprisoned in Russia in connection with their work. France has ordered Russian media commentator Xenia Fedorova to leave the country, the interior ministry said on Wednesday, accusing her of churning out Kremlin propaganda. Fedorova was placed under house arrest, according to a source close to the case. Fedorova used to run the French arm of the Kremlin propaganda channel RT, now banned in France. She appears on the CNews television channel and Europe 1 radio, and writes for Le Journal du Dimanche newspaper, spreading Kremlin talking points about Ukraine and the West. The French newspaper Liberation cited the expulsion order as accusing Fedorova of acting “as a conduit for disinformation campaigns orchestrated by the Russian authorities” with the aim of “destabilising public order” in France. Fedorova’s lawyer Emmanuel Piwnica told AFP on Wednesday that his client would “immediately” file an appeal. In a joint statement, Canal+, owner of CNews, and Lagardere, which owns Europe 1, said diversity of opinion was important for democratic debate. Members of the centrist Renew group in the European parliament have called on the European Union to impose sanctions on Fedorova, describing her as a “well-known Russian propagandist”. Ukraine said it had appealed against the International Olympic Committee’s decision to ease restrictions on Russian athletes, arguing the move is premature and violated the Olympic Charter. The IOC lifted its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee earlier this month, while simultaneously scrapping a range of restrictions on Russian athletes introduced over Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
chineseTitle: 乌克兰战争简报：F-16在追逐俄罗斯空中目标时坠毁
chineseSummary: 飞行员在“故障”后发现安全并被送往医疗；俄罗斯无人机公司负责人中枪。第 1,618 天我们所知道的
chineseContent: 乌克兰空军周三宣布，一架 F-16 战斗机在前线执行任务时坠毁，飞行员安全弹射。这架飞机在执行拦截俄罗斯空中目标任务时发生故障。飞行员被发现安全并被送往医院接受治疗。专家们正在检查坠机现场。乌克兰已从荷兰和丹麦等北约国家接收了F-16。俄罗斯一家无人机制造商的董事兼创始人周三早些时候被枪杀，检察官称这是一起“谋杀未遂”。安德烈·切列佐夫 (Andrei Cherezov) 是俄罗斯航空运输实验室的负责人，该实验室因开发“Ovod”系列作战无人机而闻名。据俄罗斯《消息报》报道，切列佐夫凌晨 1 点左右下班回家，在莫斯科以南约 150 公里（90 英里）的图拉遭到身份不明的袭击者袭击。乌克兰军队周二晚上袭击了俄罗斯最大的两家炼油厂：俄罗斯彼尔姆地区的一家卢克石油公司炼油厂，距离乌克兰超过 1,500 公里（900 英里），以及梁赞的一家炼油厂，距离边境约 400 公里（180 英里）。乌克兰安全部门和军事总参谋部宣布了此次袭击。据乌克兰称，这些炼油厂的年产能合计约为 2.2 亿桶石油。乌克兰最近几天瞄准的俄罗斯在线零售商 Wildberry 表示，该公司已从梁赞的一家工厂疏散员工。俄罗斯最大的银行储蓄银行正忙于重组贷款并弥补因乌克兰无人机袭击这家电子商务公司而造成的贷款损失。俄罗斯联邦储蓄银行表示，袭击发生后，在线零售商和供应商的信用质量恶化，约有 300 家公司寻求重组贷款。俄罗斯联邦储蓄银行向 Wildberry 和竞争对手 Ozon 提供贷款，后者的 f
